title: Lior and the Wreck
premise: Elodie Delacroix, a mountain guide blacklisted after a disaster she may or may not have caused, is broke and desperate when a dying prospector named Lior trades her a map to a wrecked expedition plane in exchange for a promise: bring the survivors' ledger home, tell no one what it found. The map leads her into the high passes with a ragged party of clients — among them a journalist hunting the same story and a man who helped bury it. As weather, sabotage, and old enemies close in, Elodie discovers the 'wreck' carried evidence of a mining company's massacre of an indigenous village, and that her own blacklist was engineered to silence anyone who might find it. In the end Elodie must choose between the promise (silence) and justice (truth), burning the map but delivering the ledger to the victims' descendants — clearing her name at the cost of the only life she knew.
about_author: Sebastian Whitlock is the pen name of a former alpine rescue volunteer who now writes adventure fiction from a cabin above the tree line. His novels are known for brutal mountain realism and morally tangled heroes who owe more than they can pay.

chapters.title: The Weight of Names
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Blacklisted and broke in a border town, she takes a last-ditch job leading a mismatched client group over the Verren Pass. A tavern confrontation reveals how thoroughly her reputation has been poisoned. Emotional beat: humiliation hardening into resolve.

chapters.title: A Dying Man's Bargain
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. The prospector Lior, gut-shot and freezing, stumbles into her camp and offers a map to a wrecked expedition plane in exchange for one promise: carry the ledger out, tell no one what it found. He dies at dawn. Emotional beat: dread wrapped in obligation.

chapters.title: Clients and Liars
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. She meets her party: a charming journalist named Corvin, a silent ex-miner called Brase, a wealthy widow, and a teenage runaway. Each has a reason for this route; none are honest about it. Emotional beat: wary suspicion beneath professional courtesy.

chapters.title: The First Ascent
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. The climb begins; Elodie tests her clients on a glacier crossing and quietly realizes Brase moves like someone trained for exactly this terrain. Emotional beat: competence as comfort, unease underneath.

chapters.title: What Lior Carried
chapters.summary: Corvin's POV. Corvin privately examines his own notes on the vanished Delacroix expedition and realizes Elodie herself was its guide — the woman he came to expose. Emotional beat: ambition wrestling with conscience.

chapters.title: The Pass Closes
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. An early storm seals the high route, forcing the party onto Lior's marked detour — straight toward the wreck. Someone has cut their rope cache. Emotional beat: the dawning certainty that they were led here.

chapters.title: Sabotage
chapters.summary: Brase's POV. Brase confesses nothing but remembers everything: he was paid by the Halvern Mining Company to watch for anyone seeking the wreck. He didn't cut the ropes — someone else is on the mountain. Emotional beat: guilt curdling into fear.

chapters.title: The Wreck
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. They find the plane, frozen mid-scream, and inside it the ledger and photographs of a burned village. Elodie keeps the promise and says nothing aloud. Emotional beat: awe collapsing into horror.

chapters.title: Ledger of the Dead
chapters.summary: The widow Marta's POV. Marta finds the ledger first and reads names she recognizes from her late husband's business letters. She confronts Elodie alone. Emotional beat: grief discovering it had company.

chapters.title: Corvin's Story
chapters.summary: Corvin's POV. Cornered by Elodie, Corvin admits he was hired to discredit any survivor account before it surfaced — the same machinery that blacklisted her. Emotional beat: betrayal becoming alliance.

chapters.title: Whiteout
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. A killer storm traps them in a crevasse camp for three days. Rations fail, tempers snap, and the runaway teen nearly walks into the void. Emotional beat: survival stripping everyone to truth.

chapters.title: The Second Party
chapters.summary: Brase's POV. Tracks appear: Halvern's recovery team, armed, following the same map. Brase must decide whether to warn the people he was sent to betray. Emotional beat: loyalty finally outweighing payment.

chapters.title: Blood on the Icefield
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. The recovery team catches them on an icefield; a standoff turns violent, and Marta takes a bullet shielding the boy. They escape down a serac field as it collapses behind them. Emotional beat: the price of survival made literal.

chapters.title: What Elodie Did
chapters.summary: Corvin's POV. Trapped overnight, Elodie finally tells the truth of the original disaster: she led clients through a storm to save Halvern's schedule, and the deaths that blacklisted her were not hers alone. Emotional beat: confession as release.

chapters.title: Marta's Vigil
chapters.summary: Marta's POV, fading. Wounded and failing, Marta makes Elodie swear the ledger reaches the village's surviving descendants, giving her a name and a valley. Emotional beat: passing the torch with the last of her strength.

chapters.title: The Descent
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. They descend the forbidden south face, off every map, hunted. Brase uses his knowledge of Halvern's patrol routes to buy them hours. Emotional beat: fugitives becoming a family of necessity.

chapters.title: Betrayal at the Bridge
chapters.summary: The runaway's POV. At the river bridge, the teen — terrified, offered amnesty — signals the recovery team. Brase dies holding the crossing so the others can burn it. Emotional beat: heartbreak and forgiveness entangled.

chapters.title: The Valley of Names
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. They reach the indigenous village from the photographs and find the descendants, alive and waiting for decades. Elodie delivers the ledger and learns Lior was the village's son, sent to bring the truth home. Emotional beat: grief transfigured into purpose.

chapters.title: Halvern Comes Down the Mountain
chapters.summary: Corvin's POV. Halvern's men surround the valley, but Corvin has already transmitted the ledger pages from the one ridge with signal. The hunters hesitate as the story goes live worldwide. Emotional beat: truth arriving like an avalanche.

chapters.title: Justice Outside the Law
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. No court will move fast enough, so the villagers and Elodie force Halvern's director up the mountain to face the graves and the cameras. He breaks. Emotional beat: reckoning without a gavel.

chapters.title: The Burning Map
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Elodie burns Lior's map so no company can ever retrace the route, keeping half a promise and breaking the other half knowingly. Her blacklist dissolves in the scandal's wake. Emotional beat: peace purchased with loss.

chapters.title: Northward, Lightly Laden
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV, epilogue. Months later, Elodie guides again — legally, quietly — with the teen apprenticed at her side and Marta's name carved on a cairn. A letter arrives from the valley: you are welcome here always. Emotional beat: survival finally feeling like living.
